Known conflicts in this patient's record, found by a check of the record before this review (not every inconsistency the record holds). Each names the side not to rely on, where the patient's own documentation shows which side is right:

retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Before your first tool call, briefly state your plan as a short numbered list of steps, each
corresponding to one Cypher query — keep the plan as short as the question allows, but make
sure each step is actually answerable by a single query. Revise the plan if a result surprises
you (e.g. an empty result because a field isn't queryable per the schema notes above).

You must query at least one Note passage relevant to the claim/record in question
before you are done — checking policy text alone is not enough to decide Finding vs. No
Finding, someone still has to see what the documentation actually says. Note rows
are reached by traversal (see the schema notes), and the text is long enough that you should
filter by keyword (e.g. `WHERE toLower(e.text) CONTAINS toLower('meniscus')`) rather than
pulling every passage. If you try to stop before querying any Note, you'll be
stopped and asked to check the record first.

Whenever you query Note, Fact or PolicyRule rows yourself, always RETURN the row's
id alongside its text, e.g. `RETURN id(n) AS source_id, n.title AS title, n.text AS text`. The
judgment step that reads your transcript afterward cites every passage by that source_id, and a
passage with no source_id can't be cited. The skill tools already return it.

Cypher literal strings break on an unescaped apostrophe (e.g. `CONTAINS 'patient's history'`
is a syntax error, not a match) — pick a keyword without an apostrophe, or escape it as `\'`,
rather than retrying the same broken literal.

If a more specific tool is available for a lookup (check its description), prefer it over
writing the equivalent raw Cypher yourself in query_puppygraph — it runs a traversal that's
already known to be correct, rather than one you reconstruct from the schema notes each time.

Patient name, MRN, date of birth, and (for some review types) claim_number itself — even when
they appear inline inside a Note's or Fact's text, not just as their own property — are
de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] or [[CLAIM-0005]], not real values. The double
brackets are literal characters of the value, not markdown or wiki-link markup to strip out —
verified live: passing a "cleaned up" claim_number with the brackets removed as a tool argument
silently matches zero rows (the underlying property is the bracketed token, not the bare text
inside it), which then looks like the record has no data at all. Copy a token byte-for-byte,
brackets included, everywhere it's used: as a tool call argument, in Cypher, and quoted verbatim
in a citation. Never remark on the token format, guess what real value it stands for, or treat
its presence as unusual — a separate step restores the real values afterward, outside anything
you do here.

Once you've gathered the claim line detail, the governing policy, and at least one relevant
medical-record passage, stop calling tools and reply with a short plain-text note of what you
found. Do NOT render a Finding/No Finding determination yourself — a separate step decides
that from what you retrieve here. Don't fabricate or guess at data you haven't queried.

Audit DRG claim MR_01's full coding for this admission — this is ONE determination for the whole stay, not per code, but check every line below (not just the first) since any one of them can drive the claim-level determination.
This claim has 28 billed lines — DO NOT call get_condition_policy on every one of them, and don't run a separate medical-record search per code either; both will overflow the retrieval model's context window well before you reach a determination (verified: this happened on a 19-line claim). Triage first: look for the principal diagnosis, any CC/MCC-tier code, and any code whose severity/support looks contestable from the billed description alone, and spend your policy/note lookups on THOSE — a routine, clearly-supported comorbidity (e.g. well-documented chronic hypertension or diabetes with no CC/MCC flag) doesn't need its own policy lookup. Batch related terms into one keyword search where you can rather than one search per condition.

Billed diagnoses (position, code, description, POA/CC-MCC flags):
  1. A40.3 — Sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae [POA=Y, MCC]
  2. R65.21 — Severe sepsis with septic shock [POA=Y, MCC]
  3. J13 — Pneumonia due to Streptococcus pneumoniae [POA=Y, CC]
  4. J96.01 — Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia [POA=Y, MCC]
  5. J80 — Acute respiratory distress syndrome [POA=Y, MCC]
  6. N17.9 — Acute kidney failure, unspecified [POA=Y, CC]
  7. J95.851 — Ventilator associated pneumonia [POA=Y, CC]

[p.818] Attending: Dr. Marcus Bell, MD (Critical Care Medicine)
Admit: 2026-01-06 Transfer: 2026-04-11
LOS: 95 days
Reason for Admission: Septic shock and severe pneumonia with respiratory failure requiring intensive care.
Admission Diagnoses
Severe community-acquired pneumonia; septic shock; ARDS
Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses
Resolving sepsis and pneumonia; ventilator-dependent respiratory failure with tracheostomy (weaning); resolved ventilator-associated
pneumonia (Pseudomonas); acute kidney injury with renal recovery, hemodialysis discontinued; resolved atrial fibrillation;
catheter-associated right IJ DVT on anticoagulation; ICU-acquired weakness; type 2 diabetes; COPD; hypertension; hyperlipidemia.
Hospital Course
[[NAME-0010]] presented with septic shock and severe multifocal pneumonia, was intubated for hypoxemic respiratory failure, and
required norepinephrine and vasopressin. The course was complicated by ARDS managed with lung-protective ventilation and prone
positioning, oliguric acute kidney injury requiring CRRT later transitioned to intermittent hemodialysis, new-onset atrial fibrillation
controlled with amiodarone, and a hospital-acquired Pseudomonas pneumonia treated with a targeted course of cefepime after
bronchoscopy. Vasopressors were discontinued by ICU day 10. An extubation attempt failed and reintubation was required, after which a
tracheostomy was placed for prolonged ventilation and a PEG for enteral nutrition. The patient was liberated from continuous ventilator
support to trach-collar trials and then to full-day trach collar. A catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT was treated with therapeutic
anticoagulation. Renal function recovered and hemodialysis was discontinued. With intensive therapy the patient's ICU-acquired
weakness improved and the patient was mobilizing with assistance. Transfer to a long-term acute care hospital for continued
ventilator/tracheostomy weaning and rehabilitation is planned.
Physical Examination
Vitals: Tmax 37.1 degC | HR 77 | MAP 77 | RR 14 | SpO2 96%. Airway/Support: tracheostomy on trach collar. General: Alert, interactive,
comfortable; participating in therapy. HEENT: mucous membranes moist, no scleral icterus. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no
murmur; well perfused. Respiratory: Clear to diminished; good air movement; tolerating trach collar. Abdomen: soft, non-distended,
+bowel sounds; PEG site clean and dry. Extremities: pulses intact. Neuro: Alert and oriented; CAM-ICU negative; strength improving
with rehab. Skin/Lines: Skin intact; healing well; ambulating with assistance.
Laboratory Data (Pertinent)
CBC: WBC 7.6 x103/uL, Hgb 10.1 g/dL, Hct 30%, platelets 225 x109/L (neutrophils 70%). BMP: Na 136, K 4.1, Cl 105, CO2 25, BUN 24,
creatinine 1.16 mg/dL, glucose 130 mg/dL, Ca 8.7, Mg 2.2, Phos 3.6. ABG (07:00): pH 7.39 / PaCO2 36 / PaO2 91 / HCO3 24; lactate
1.2 mmol/L; P/F ratio 311. Markers: procalcitonin 3.8 ng/mL, CRP 47 mg/L, troponin 0.02 ng/mL.
Imaging (Pertinent)
No new imaging obtained today. Most recent radiograph reviewed and compared; findings consistent with the documented clinical
trajectory.
Condition & Functional Status at Transfer
Alert, oriented, and conversant with a speaking valve. Tracheostomy on trach collar (FiO2 35%). Tolerating a modified diet with
supplemental PEG feeds. Ambulates short distances with a walker and assistance. Off vasopressors and dialysis.
Transfer Medications
Medication | Dose | Route | Frequency | Indication
[p.819] Cefepime | 2 g | IV | q8h (finish course) | Resolving VAP
Apixaban | 5 mg | PO/PEG | BID | Catheter-associated DVT
Amiodarone | 200 mg | PO/PEG | Daily | Atrial fibrillation
Insulin glargine | 18 units | SC | QHS | Diabetes
Insulin aspart | sliding scale | SC | with feeds | Glycemic control
Pantoprazole | 40 mg | PO/PEG | Daily | Stress ulcer prophylaxis
Atorvastatin | 40 mg | PO/PEG | QHS | Hyperlipidemia
Metoprolol tartrate | 25 mg | PO/PEG | BID | Rate control/HTN
Acetaminophen | 650 mg | PO/PEG | q6h PRN | Pain/fever
Albuterol-ipratropium | 1 unit dose | Nebulized | q6h + PRN | COPD
Follow-Up & Recommendations
1. Continue structured trach-collar weaning; evaluate for decannulation when stable.
2. Nephrology follow-up; monitor renal function; avoid nephrotoxins.
3. Complete cefepime course; ID stewardship follow-up.
4. Continue anticoagulation for catheter-associated DVT with hematology guidance.
5. Diabetes management with feeds.
6. Intensive PT/OT and speech therapy.
7. Return precautions: fever, respiratory decompensation, bleeding, chest pain.

Arrival EMS, ground
Disposition Admit - ICU
History of Present Illness
[[NAME-0010]] is a 79-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, COPD, and prior tobacco use who presented with five
days of progressive productive cough, subjective fevers to 39.4 degC, pleuritic left-sided chest pain, and worsening dyspnea. Over the 24
hours before arrival the family noted increasing lethargy, confusion, and reduced oral intake. On EMS assessment the patient was
hypotensive (systolic 82 mmHg) and hypoxemic (SpO2 84% on room air) and was placed on high-flow nasal cannula. In the ED the
patient met criteria for septic shock with a lactate of 5.1 mmol/L that failed to clear after a 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid bolus. Given
profound hypoxemic respiratory failure and depressed mental status the patient underwent rapid-sequence intubation, and
broad-spectrum antimicrobials and vasopressor support were initiated.
Past Medical / Surgical History
[p.695] Medical: Type 2 diabetes (last A1c 8.4%), essential hypertension, COPD (GOLD 2, former 30 pack-year smoker), hyperlipidemia,
obesity (BMI 30.2), remote pneumonia. Surgical: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy; inguinal hernia repair.
Social / Family History
Lives with spouse; warehouse supervisor. Former smoker; social alcohol; no illicit drugs. Family history of coronary disease and diabetes.
Review of Systems
Constitutional: fevers, chills, fatigue. Respiratory: cough, sputum, dyspnea, pleuritic pain. Neuro: confusion, somnolence. GI: reduced
intake, nausea. Remaining systems limited by clinical condition.
Physical Examination (on presentation)
Vitals: 39.3 degC | HR 128 | BP 82/49 (MAP 60) | RR 30 | SpO2 84% RA. General: toxic-appearing, diaphoretic, obtunded (GCS 10).
HEENT: dry mucous membranes; no meningismus. Cardiac: tachycardic, regular, no murmur. Respiratory: marked WOB; coarse
crackles L base; diffuse rhonchi. Abdomen: soft, non-distended, no guarding. Neuro: GCS 10 (E2 V3 M5), no focal deficit. Skin: warm,
mottled knees, cap refill 4 s.
Laboratory Data
WBC 22.4 x103/uL (89% neutrophils); Hgb 12.8; platelets 92 x109/L; Na 134, K 4.6, CO2 18, BUN 42, creatinine 3.1 mg/dL (AKI); glucose
214; lactate 5.1 mmol/L; procalcitonin 24.6 ng/mL; ABG pH 7.22 / PaCO2 41 / PaO2 58 on HFNC. Influenza/RSV/SARS-CoV-2 multiplex
negative.
Imaging (Pertinent)
Chest Radiograph, Portable AP: Multifocal pneumonia, left greater than right. Support devices appropriately positioned. See the
Diagnostic Imaging section for the full report.
Active Problem List
# | Problem
1 | Septic shock secondary to severe community-acquired pneumonia
2 | Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), moderate-severe
3 | Acute hypoxemic and hypercapnic respiratory failure - mechanical ventilation
4 | Acute kidney injury requiring renal replacement therapy (CRRT then IHD)
5 | Ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas aeruginosa), hospital day 6
6 | New-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
7 | ICU-acquired delirium (hyperactive/mixed)
8 | Critical illness myopathy / ICU-acquired weakness
9 | Catheter-associated deep vein thrombosis (right IJ)
10 | Type 2 diabetes mellitus with stress hyperglycemia
11 | Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
12 | Essential hypertension / hyperlipidemia
13 | Obesity (BMI 30.2)
Assessment
79-year-old woman with severe multifocal community-acquired pneumonia complicated by septic shock, hypoxemic respiratory failure
meeting ARDS criteria, acute kidney injury, and sepsis-associated encephalopathy. High illness severity; admitted to MICU.
Plan
1. Sepsis/CAP: vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam + azithromycin; cultures; source imaging.
2. Respiratory: lung-protective ventilation (ARDSnet); consider proning.
3. Shock: norepinephrine to MAP >= 65; vasopressin if refractory; central/arterial access.
4. AKI: avoid nephrotoxins; nephrology; anticipate RRT.
5. Glycemic: insulin infusion.
6. Prophylaxis: VTE, stress ulcer.

Admission Orders
Admit: MICU. Condition: critical. Vitals: continuous telemetry, arterial-line BP, SpO2; hourly assessment; strict I/O.
Ventilation: ARDSnet low-tidal-volume protocol (6 mL/kg IBW), plateau <= 30, titrate PEEP/FiO2, SpO2 90-96%.
Hemodynamics: norepinephrine to MAP >= 65; add vasopressin if > 0.3 mcg/kg/min; stress-dose steroids if refractory.
Antimicrobials: vancomycin (AUC), piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h extended infusion, azithromycin 500 mg IV daily.
Labs: CBC/CMP/ABG/lactate q6h until stable; cultures x2, sputum, urine; procalcitonin.

Patient: [[NAME-0010]]
Date: 2026-04-11
Destination: Long-Term Acute Care Hospital
Why You Are Being Transferred: You are being moved to a long-term acute care hospital to continue weaning from the
breathing machine and tracheostomy and to keep working on your strength.
Your Diagnoses (Plain Language)
You had a serious lung infection (pneumonia) that led to sepsis and required a breathing machine, kidney support (dialysis), and time in
the ICU. Your infection and kidneys have improved, and you now have a tracheostomy and a feeding tube while you continue to recover.
Medicines
Take all medicines exactly as listed on your medication sheet. This includes an antibiotic to finish, a blood thinner for a clot, a
heart-rhythm medicine, insulin for diabetes, a stomach-protection medicine, a cholesterol medicine, and breathing treatments. Do not
stop the blood thinner unless your doctor tells you to.
Activity
Keep working with physical and occupational therapy every day. Move and walk as much as the team allows, with help. Change positions
often to protect your skin.
Diet & Feeding
Follow the diabetic, kidney-friendly diet. You may take some foods/liquids by mouth as cleared by speech therapy, with tube feeds
through your PEG for the rest of your nutrition. Flush the tube as instructed.
Devices, Lines & Wounds
Keep the tracheostomy clean and humidified. Suction as taught. Continue trach-collar and capping trials as directed by respiratory
therapy.
Equipment / Supplies Arranged
Tracheostomy care supplies and suction, feeding-tube supplies and pump, glucose monitor, and mobility aid (walker) - coordinated
through the receiving facility and DME vendor.
Follow-Up Appointments
Specialty | When | Purpose
Pulmonology | Per LTAC schedule | Ventilator/trach weaning, decannulation
Nephrology | Within 1-2 weeks | Kidney recovery monitoring
Infectious Diseases | Per LTAC | Complete antibiotic course
Primary Care | After LTAC discharge | Overall care, medication review
Hematology / Anticoagulation | Within 1-2 weeks | Blood thinner management
When to Get Help Immediately
Call for help right away for: fever, trouble breathing or increased secretions, the tracheostomy coming out or blocking, chest pain,
bleeding, confusion, or feeding-tube problems (leaking, blockage, or the tube coming out).

Why You Are Being Transferred: You are being moved to a long-term acute care hospital to continue weaning from the

You had a serious lung infection (pneumonia) that led to sepsis and required a breathing machine, kidney support (dialysis), and time in

heart-rhythm medicine, insulin for diabetes, a stomach-protection medicine, a cholesterol medicine, and breathing treatments. Do not
stop the blood thinner unless your doctor tells you to.

Keep working with physical and occupational therapy every day. Move and walk as much as the team allows, with help. Change positions
often to protect your skin.
Diet & Feeding
Follow the diabetic, kidney-friendly diet. You may take some foods/liquids by mouth as cleared by speech therapy, with tube feeds
through your PEG for the rest of your nutrition. Flush the tube as instructed.
Devices, Lines & Wounds
Keep the tracheostomy clean and humidified. Suction as taught. Continue trach-collar and capping trials as directed by respiratory
therapy.
Equipment / Supplies Arranged
Tracheostomy care supplies and suction, feeding-tube supplies and pump, glucose monitor, and mobility aid (walker) - coordinated
through the receiving facility and DME vendor.
Follow-Up Appointments
Specialty | When | Purpose
Pulmonology | Per LTAC schedule | Ventilator/trach weaning, decannulation
Nephrology | Within 1-2 weeks | Kidney recovery monitoring
Infectious Diseases | Per LTAC | Complete antibiotic course
Primary Care | After LTAC discharge | Overall care, medication review
Hematology / Anticoagulation | Within 1-2 weeks | Blood thinner management

judge_messages.content:
You are a senior clinical claims auditor deciding a determination for one
billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a
claims/medical-record/policy knowledge graph for this line — the Cypher queries run and the
rows each one returned. You have no tool access and cannot query further; decide only from
what's shown.

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Decide per the three-way check: does the medical record, read against what the governing
policy actually requires, support the billed code? Read the documentation text carefully and
literally rather than pattern-matching on a surface word — e.g. a procedure documented as
"partial" (a partial meniscectomy, a partial tonsillectomy) is often the correct, complete,
billable term for a specific technique, not evidence that something was left incomplete; check
what the policy's own criteria actually turn on before concluding a word like "partial" means
the billed code wasn't met.

Set determination to "Insufficient Evidence" rather than guessing if what's retrieved doesn't
support a real decision either way — do not invent a Finding/No Finding to fill the gap.

system_note is the auditor note a human reviewer reads on EVERY claim, Finding or not — write
it with explicit citations (document/section/page) and reasoning a reviewer could audit line by
line; a correct determination with a
vague, citation-free note still scores as a weak note (see the quality bar in the schema
field's own description).

rationale_letter is a SEPARATE, formal appeal-ready letter to the provider — only written when
determination is Finding (null otherwise). It restates the finding and its basis for an
external, non-technical reader, not a repeat of system_note's internal auditor reasoning.

Page numbers: a medical-record note can span several PDF pages, and its page_start/page_end
are not the page of any particular line in it. In a long note's text, a [p.N] marker means the
text after it (up to the next marker) is on physical page N; cite that page in system_note,
never a note's page_start/page_end range. A note whose page_start equals its page_end is all on
that page. In a multi-page note with no marker before the line, name the note without a page.

evidence_cited must reference only passages that actually appear in the retrieved rows above.
Each entry is the source_id of the one row the quote comes from, copied exactly, and the quote
copied verbatim from that row's text, character for character: don't wrap part of it in
quotation marks, fix a typo, or drop a word or code from the middle. Never invent or recall one. Code checks each quote
against that row and fills in the document, section and page from it, so a quote that isn't in
the cited row, or a source_id that wasn't retrieved, is dropped. Each quote is ONE contiguous
passage from a single row: if you need two separate passages, give two separate evidence_cited
entries rather than joining them with "..."; a stitched-together quote can't be verified. Rows
with no source_id (claim lines, code descriptions, a tool's own summary rows) aren't citable;
cite the record or policy row behind them instead.

Patient name, MRN, and date of birth appear as de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] —
including inline inside quoted note/fact text — not real values. Reproduce them exactly as
given in system_note, rationale_letter, and evidence_cited quotes; a separate step restores
the real values afterward. Never remark on the token format or guess/reconstruct what it stands
for.

discharge_disposition, finding_reason, recovery_type, skilled_services,
adjusted_date_of_service, corrected_revenue_code, adjusted_units_billed,
revised_diagnosis_set, and revised_procedure_set are only meaningful for specific review types
(DRG, Readmission, SNF, SNF, SNF, SNF, DRG, and DRG respectively) — see each field's own schema
description and this review type's domain notes above to know whether to populate it; leave it
null when this review type doesn't call for it.

If this is a DRG review: you are deciding for the WHOLE claim in one pass, not one line — check
every diagnosis and procedure line given to you (POA, CC/MCC tier, whether it's still
supported), not just the one the question happens to name first. revised_diagnosis_set and
revised_procedure_set must each be the claim's COMPLETE corrected list (every code that should
remain billed, in the same shape as what you were given, position 1 = principal diagnosis) —
not a delta of only the line(s) that changed. code_decisions is what's scored: one entry per
billed code, each exactly once, plus additions, with the POA and CC/MCC tier each diagnosis
should carry, and the evidence_cited IDs behind every change. Code checks it and builds the
corrected lists from it.

result.system_note: Audit summary (claim MR_01): The record supports organism-specific sepsis (A40.3) with septic shock (R65.21), acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (J96.01) and ARDS (J80), and documents ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) due to Pseudomonas that developed after intubation. However, several billed elements are incorrect: J95.851 (ventilator-associated pneumonia) was billed POA=Y and as CC but the chart documents VAP developing during the admission and the VAP policy classifies J95.851 as MCC with POA=N; Z99.2 (dependence on renal dialysis) remains billed despite the medical record stating hemodialysis was discontinued before transfer; I21.4 (NSTEMI) is coded without documentation of a provider diagnosis of NSTEMI. Key supporting citations used below (document / section / page): - Provider admission H&P documents septic shock with lactate 5.1 and immediate intubation (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n9, H&P, p.770) (ev1). - Infectious Diseases consult documents organism identification: admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n50, ID consult, p.139) (ev2). - Physician orders / MAR show vasopressor administration (norepinephrine administered) supporting septic shock (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n520, Orders, p.258) (ev3). - Chest radiograph documents multifocal/lobar consolidation consistent with pneumonia and later progression (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n12, Diagnostic Imaging, p.416) (ev4). - Discharge / Transfer Summary explicitly documents: resolved VAP (Pseudomonas); renal recovery with hemodialysis discontinued; ventilator-dependent respiratory failure with tracheostomy - supporting VAP diagnosis and showing dialysis was stopped prior to transfer (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n829, Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.818) (ev5). - Progress note documents new right infiltrate with purulent secretions and VAP suspected on hospital day 6 (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n49, Critical Care Progress Note, p.139) (ev6). - Physician orders document CRRT initiation (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n520, Orders, p.258) and later notes/Problem List document renal recovery (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n5, Hospital Problem List, p.455) (ev7, ev9). - Cardiology consult documents the atrial arrhythmia as secondary/reversible (NOT diagnostic of NSTEMI) (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n37, Cardiology Consult, p.639) (ev8). - The governing VAP policy explicitly lists J95.851 as Ventilator associated pneumonia [MCC] and requires VAP onset >48 hours after intubation and POA=N (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.docx-b8) (ev10). Reasoned determinations line-by-line (examples): - A40.3 (Sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae): keep as principal. Supported by ID culture result (ev2) and inpatient sepsis documentation (ev1). - R65.21 (Severe sepsis with septic shock): keep as additional MCC; vasopressors and elevated lactate are documented (ev3, ev1) and the policy requires R65.21 to be reported with organism-specific A40.-/A41.- when criteria are met. - J95.851 (Ventilator-associated pneumonia): keep but correct POA to N and severity to MCC. Provider and ID notes document VAP developing on hospital day 6 with bronchoscopy and targeted therapy (ev6, ev2, ev5); policy requires POA=N and classifies J95.851 as MCC (ev10). The originally-billed POA=Y and CC tier are incorrect. - Z99.2 (Dependence on renal dialysis): remove. The record documents CRRT initiation (ev7) but also documents renal recovery with hemodialysis discontinued prior to transfer (ev9, ev5); dependence on dialysis was not a persistent discharge status and should not remain an active dependence code. - I21.4 (NSTEMI): remove. Cardiology consultation characterizes troponin elevation and atrial arrhythmia as secondary to sepsis/catecholamines and does not diagnose NSTEMI; discharge summary and problem list do not list NSTEMI (ev8, ev5). - 7204 (claim line artifact / not a valid ICD-10 code): remove. This appears to be an invalid/errant claim-line entry and is not reflected in the clinician documentation of active problems (ev5). All kept diagnosis/procedure codes and POA/severity assignments are listed in the revised code sets below with the evidence items supporting each change named in code_decisions. Auditor action: remove invalid code 7204; change POA for J95.851 to N and upgrade its severity to MCC; remove Z99.2 and I21.4. result.rationale_letter: Re: DRG audit determination - Claim MR_01 Dear Provider/Coding Team, We completed an audit of the inpatient DRG coding for claim MR_01 (admit 2026-01-06 to 2026-04-11). The medical record documents a severe infectious pulmonary presentation with septic shock and respiratory failure requiring intubation, prolonged mechanical ventilation, tracheostomy, CRRT/HD for AKI, and an ICU course complicated by ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas). Our findings and the corrections we are making are summarized below. Finding (required correction) 1. Ventilator-associated pneumonia (J95.851) - POA indicator and severity tier incorrect: The chart documents VAP developing on hospital day 6 (ICU progress note: "Interval: fever recrudescence, rising WBC, purulent secretions and new right infiltrate - VAP suspected" and ID consult: "Severe CAP complicated by day-6 VAP") and the discharge summary documents "resolved ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas)" (supporting citations: Critical Care Progress Note and ID Consult; Discharge/Transfer Summary). Per the governing VAP policy, J95.851 is a ventilator-associated pneumonia diagnosis (MCC) that requires onset greater than 48 hours after intubation and must be assigned POA = N (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8). The claim originally carried POA=Y and was assigned as CC; we are correcting the POA to N and the severity to MCC. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n49 (Progress Note, p.139); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n50 (ID consult, p.139); NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_01.pdf-n829 (Discharge/Transfer Summary, p.818); RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b8. 2. Z99.2 (Dependence on renal dialysis) - removal: Although CRRT/hemodialysis was pursued for sepsis-associated AKI (Physician Orders show CRRT initiation), the discharge documentation and problem list document renal recovery and that hemodialysis was discontinued prior to transfer ("AKI requiring RRT ... Resolved | Renal recovery day 24; HD DC'd" and Discharge Summary: "hemodialysis discontinued"). Dependence on dialysis (Z99.2) should not remain active when dialysis dependence has resolved. code_decisions.reason: 7204 is not a valid ICD-10 diagnosis code and is not reflected in clinician documentation of active problems or discharge diagnoses; remove as claim artifact. Discharge summary lists active/resolved problems and does not include any code-like '7204' (ev5).

Progress notes and ID consult document ventilator-associated pneumonia developing after intubation (VAP suspected on hospital day 6) with Pseudomonas identified and treated (ev6, ev2, ev5). Governing VAP policy classifies J95.851 as MCC and requires POA = N when VAP develops during admission (ev10). The originally billed POA=Y and CC tier are incorrect and are corrected here.
Discharge summary and progress/ID notes document Pseudomonas as the organism for the hospital-acquired pneumonia/VAP (ev5, ev6); keep organism specification with POA = N.
Cardiology documents new-onset atrial fibrillation in the setting of sepsis (ev8); code is hospital-acquired (POA=N) and remains a CC.
Discharge summary documents catheter-associated right IJ DVT and anticoagulation at discharge (ev5).

Discharge summary documents tracheostomy with ongoing trach-collar weaning and ventilator-dependent respiratory failure at transfer (ev5); retain dependence-on-respirator status with POA=N (developed during stay).

Although CRRT/HD was initiated (ev7), the problem list and discharge summary document renal recovery and that hemodialysis was discontinued (ev9, ev5). Dependence on dialysis (Z99.2) should be removed because it had resolved by discharge.

Cardiology describes troponin elevation and arrhythmia as secondary to sepsis/catecholamines and does not diagnose NSTEMI; discharge summary does not list NSTEMI (ev8, ev5). No provider-authored NSTEMI diagnosis to support I21.4.
Endotracheal intubation performed on admission for respiratory failure (H&P and orders document intubation and vasopressors).
Central venous catheter (right IJ) placed for vasopressors and access (orders and discharge summary reflect central line placement and catheter-associated DVT).
Arterial line placement documented in orders for continuous hemodynamic monitoring.
Femoral dialysis catheter placed for CRRT (orders and dialysis documentation).
Bronchoscopy with BAL performed for VAP diagnosis (orders and ID/progress notes).
Percutaneous dilational tracheostomy performed per procedure orders and discharge summary documenting tracheostomy and trach-collar weaning.
PEG tube placement performed (orders and discharge instructions reference PEG feeds).
Assistance with respiratory ventilation >96 consecutive hours is supported by intubation, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and tracheostomy with ongoing weaning at transfer.
Urinary filtration / dialysis procedures (CRRT then IHD) are documented in orders and discharge/problem-list materials.
